title: How Rush Injury Law Stopped Writing Settlement Checks
summary: Rush Injury Law pays clients electronically from trust with Hona Disbursements. Less check writing, faster payouts, and less fraud risk. Read the story.
body_markdown:
Every personal injury firm knows the last mile of a settlement. The case is won, the funds land in trust, and then someone still has to write the check, sign it, mail it, and wait. Then the client calls asking where the money is.


Rush Injury Law, a Northern California personal injury firm with offices across the Bay Area and Sacramento, decided that last mile should be the easy part. So the firm moved its client settlement payouts to Hona Disbursements.


## The problem: paper checks at the finish line


Checks feel safe because they are familiar. But they come with a lot of manual work. Someone writes each one, someone signs each one, and someone gets it out the door. Multiply that across every settlement and it adds up fast.


And checks carry risk of their own. A check in the mail can be lost, stolen, or altered, and the client often does not find out for a week or two.


## The change: paying clients electronically from trust


With Hona Disbursements, the firm drafts the payout inside Hona and an approver signs off. The client gets a text from the firm's own number with a secure link. They verify their identity and choose how to get paid: instantly to a debit card in seconds or minutes, or by free direct deposit in 4 to 6 business days. Money moves through Hona's payments partner, Confido Legal.


Jim Rush, Owner of Rush Injury Law, put it simply:


> "I can't believe we haven't been doing this before. It's cut down the work we were doing by manually writing, signing, and transmitting checks to clients. Most clients absolutely love the option to get their money right away."


> "It makes my life easier. The less checks I have to sign, the better."


## The worry: is electronic payment from trust safe?


This is the first question most firms ask. Jim's answer is that the old way is the bigger risk:


> "People get scared about electronic payments from the trust account, but checks to clients are even worse. People can wash those checks, and pretty soon you've got fraud all over your account. That's a bigger risk, in my opinion."


Every payout goes through an approval step before any money moves, and the client verifies their identity before accepting it. No paper sitting in a mailbox.


## The takeaway


Rush Injury Law spends less time writing and signing checks, and their clients get paid faster. If your accounting team is still printing settlement checks,[book a demo](https://www.hona.com/demo) and see how Hona Disbursements works.
